cap:actor-runners: How troupe runs an actor through an out-of-process runner: launching it, supervising the run within named limits, cancelling it, and deriving one trustworthy outcome per run.
cap:artifact-store: Content-addressed storage for run artifacts that are too large or too sensitive for git, such as raw transcripts, so that lineage can reference them by hash and any copy can be verified.
cap:cli: The command-line surface of troupe: a thin client over the core's commands and queries, covering how it is invoked, how global flags are parsed, and how results and errors are rendered and reported through exit codes.
cap:client-protocol: Defines the commands and queries every surface uses to reach troupe's core: language-neutral messages that the CLI calls in process today and a run server will serve later, so no behaviour exists in only one surface.
cap:docs-publishing: How a change to troupe reaches troupe.run: which pushes notify the website to rebuild `/docs`, and what the job that sends the notice may do.
cap:event-store: Records troupe's events as append-only text that git can merge without conflicts, and reads them back in a stable local order that meets the `eventsourcing` library's recorder contract, across branches, merges and forks.
cap:flake-hunt: Finding flaky tests on demand, on every platform: repeating tests in overlapping rounds, under optional load and with fresh randomised inputs, and reporting each failure with the evidence an issue needs.
cap:identity: Works out who is acting, through an ordered, pluggable chain of identity sources, so that every event names a real actor and troupe fails rather than guesses when nobody can be identified.
cap:lineage: Makes every event troupe records explain itself: who made it, through what, when, why, as part of which change, with whose approval, and in what version-control state, so history can always be traced and trusted.
cap:platform: The single seam for OS-specific behaviour, so that troupe's file writes, locking, child processes, interrupts, directory watching and path display behave the same on Linux, macOS and Windows. Later: daemon IPC.
cap:policy: Gives troupe one seam through which every policy setting is read, each with a named default and a known source, so policy can grow levels and combinators later without anything else reading policy its own way.
cap:protocol: The rules every schema troupe publishes follows, in `protocol/` and in each plugin: JSON Schema that is strict, so every value troupe reads or writes has a known shape that tools, editors and other languages can check.
cap:python-support: Which Python versions troupe supports, how that support is declared and enforced, and how the declaration stays exactly in step with the versions CI tests.
cap:quality-check: What troupe's `scripts/check.py` runs, the scoped form that narrows its tests, and troupe's declaration of which paths need which part of the check. The commit guard and CI read that declaration, and every test run keeps it true.
cap:releases: How troupe's packages get their versions, changelogs and releases: all derived from the Conventional Commits on `main` through a release pull request, never edited by hand.
cap:runner-protocol: The language-neutral contract between troupe and an actor runner, so that a runner can be written in any language and troupe can run any actor (Claude Code, a local model, a scripted runner) the same way.
cap:runs: Records each run of an actor in the theatre's event store, with lineage, from its first runner event to its derived outcome, and reads runs back as projections so a person can see what is happening and what happened.
cap:scripted-runner: A deterministic actor runner for tests: it plays a script or replays a recorded stream through the runner contract, so every run outcome can be produced on demand, offline and for free.
cap:stages: Defines where an actor runs and whether troupe can enforce what it may touch there: the stage port, and the local stage, which can't enforce any effect and so runs an actor only when policy allows it.
cap:user-docs: troupe's user documentation, which troupe.run's `/docs` is built from: where it lives, the page contract the site builds from, which reference is generated and how it's kept true, how pages describe built and unbuilt behaviour, and the vocabulary rules they follow.
cap:vcs: The version-control port troupe reads the working tree's state through, so the event store and lineage work the same whether a theatre uses git or no version control at all.
